user_input: Why is the decoder self-attention masked, and how is the masking implemented?
retrieved_contexts:
['This mimics the
typical encoder-decoder attention mechanisms in sequence-to-sequence models such as
[31, 2, 8]. • The encoder contains self-attention layers. In a self-attention layer all of the keys, values
and queries come from the same place, in this case, the output of the previous layer in the
encoder. Each position in the encoder can attend to all positions in the previous layer of the
encoder. • Similarly, self-attention layers in the decoder allow each position in the decoder to attend to
all positions in the decoder up to and including that position. We need to prevent leftward
information ﬂow in the decoder to preserve the auto-regressive property. We implement this
inside of scaled dot-product attention by masking out (setting to −∞) all values in the input
of the softmax which correspond to illegal connections. See Figure 2.', 'We also modify the self-attention
sub-layer in the decoder stack to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions.']
response: The decoder self-attention is masked to prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions, preserving the auto-regressive property. This is implemented by masking out (setting to −∞) all values in the input of the softmax which correspond to illegal connections in the scaled dot-product attention mechanism.
reference: Masking prevents positions from attending to subsequent positions, so that (together with output embeddings offset by one position) the prediction for position i depends only on known outputs at positions less than i, preserving the auto-regressive property. It is implemented inside scaled dot-product attention by setting to -infinity all softmax inputs that correspond to illegal (leftward) connections.

response: To counteract the effect of large magnitudes of dot products for larger values of \( d_k \), the Transformer scales the dot products by \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}} \). This scaling helps to stabilize the gradients in the softmax function, which can become extremely small when the dot products grow large.
